holes_found.location: detail_evidence, argument (iv) parenthetical (Bessel-mode escape), sentence ending '...that is π · R_Earth by the AE-projection identity — the same AE-projection identity is imported a second time.'
holes_found.description: EXP-648 patch 1 replaced the repeated 'globe fingerprint' phrase with 'the same AE-projection identity is imported a second time' to fix a cross-paragraph terminology repetition. But the immediately preceding clause in the SAME sentence already reads '...by the AE-projection identity — the same AE-projection identity is imported a second time.' This puts the term 'AE-projection identity' twice back-to-back in one sentence, separated only by an em-dash -- an intra-sentence repetition that reads at least as awkwardly as the cross-paragraph 'globe fingerprint' repetition the patch was meant to fix. WIN-038.c12 (the prior curmudgeon-verify pass on this same EXP) passed Check 5 on this sentence with the justification 'ties back to the AE-projection identity named two clauses earlier' -- that description is inaccurate: the term's first true introduction is in argument (ii), a different argument entirely, not 'two clauses earlier.' The two AE-projection identity mentions actually adjacent to each other are the ones newly juxtaposed by this patch, within argument (iv)'s own sentence.
holes_found.suggested_fix: Reword the second occurrence to avoid literal repetition, e.g. '...requires the same a = 20,015 km that is π · R_Earth by construction — the AE-projection identity is imported a second time' (drop 'the same' before the second mention, or replace the second mention with a pronoun / shorter callback like 'that identity').
